ayeaye: An aye-aye, a strange lemur sitting upright on a branch, with shaggy black-brown fur, huge orange staring eyes, prominent rodent front teeth, and one extremely long thin skeletal MIDDLE FINGER held out. Its ears are ROUND THIN DARK EARS as big as its own face, standing straight up on top of its head like a mouse's ears scaled up enormously. It has FOUR ORDINARY LIMBS AND NOTHING ELSE - two arms and two legs, NO WINGS, NO MEMBRANE, NO FLAPS OF SKIN between its limbs and its body. EXACTLY ONE TAIL: a single long bushy tail, one only
saiga: ONE SINGLE SAIGA ANTELOPE ALONE, ONE HEAD, ONE NECK, ONE PAIR OF HORNS - a solitary animal, no second animal, no companion, nothing behind it. A pale sandy antelope standing on four legs in side-on three-quarter view, its head turned toward the viewer. Its muzzle is SWOLLEN AND PUFFY like a soft rubber ball stuck on the front of its face, with the two nostril holes opening DOWNWARD toward the ground. The swelling ends level with its mouth and goes no lower. Two ribbed amber horns, large dark eyes, stocky body, slim legs
kudu: A greater kudu bull standing on EXACTLY FOUR LEGS - four legs and no more, two in front and two behind, each one clearly separate. A very tall slender grey-brown antelope with long thin legs, a deep narrow chest, a long neck and very large rounded ears. Six to eight narrow WHITE VERTICAL STRIPES down each flank and a white chevron between the eyes. Its two horns rise UP AND AWAY FROM THE HEAD in a wide open corkscrew, each twist as wide across as the animal's own skull, spiralling upward like an open drill bit. The horns must NOT curl down and around beside the cheeks, and must NOT form a tight ring against the head
dikdik: A dik-dik standing on four legs, the smallest antelope in the world - NO BIGGER THAN A DOMESTIC CAT, with the stubby proportions of a very small animal: a short rounded body, SHORT legs no longer than its own body is deep, and a HEAD THAT LOOKS TOO BIG FOR ITS BODY. Enormous dark eyes taking up much of its face, a dark tear-mark slit below each eye, a tuft of hair on the forehead, and two tiny straight spike horns SHORTER THAN ITS OWN EARS. A plain slightly pointed muzzle. It should look like a toy-sized antelope, never like a full-grown gazelle
leopardseal: A leopard seal seen in full side view against nothing at all, its body a strong dark shape with no pale scenery around it. A long sleek muscular seal with a serpentine reptilian head and a long neck, lying stretched out flat with its belly down. Its back is CHARCOAL BLUE-GREY, clearly darker than any background, fading to a CREAM-WHITE throat and belly, and it is COVERED IN SCATTERED BLACK SPOTS, densest along the flanks and across the pale throat. Long fore-flippers, wide mouth closed. NO ICE, NO SNOW, NO WATER, NO GROUND, NO SCENERY BEHIND IT
weedyseadragon: A weedy seadragon, a slender fish held HORIZONTALLY WITH ITS TAIL STRETCHED OUT STRAIGHT BEHIND IT, drifting level like a floating twig. Its tail is STRAIGHT AND TAPERING and must NOT curl, must NOT coil, must NOT hook - it does not grip anything. SMALL LEAF-SHAPED FLAPS OF SKIN sprout all along its back, belly and tail like scraps of torn seaweed, and these leafy flaps are the most important feature of the animal. A long straight tubular snout, a thin body ringed with bony bands, reddish-orange skin crossed by purple-blue bands and dotted with bright yellow spots. NOT a seahorse, NOT upright, NOT curled
oarfish: An oarfish, a fish shaped like a LONG SILVER RIBBON OR BELT - as narrow from top to bottom as a person's forearm but many many times longer, flattened flat like a strap of foil, curving in loose S-shaped waves. Its body TAPERS AWAY TO A THIN POINT at the back end with NO TAIL FIN AT ALL - there is no fan, no fork, no spread tail, the body simply narrows to nothing. Silvery skin flecked with dark spots, a BRIGHT CRIMSON DORSAL FIN of short rays running the entire length of its back, a TALL CREST OF LONG RED PLUMES rising from the top of its head, and two long trailing red oar-shaped fins. A small blunt head with a large dark eye
baskingshark: A basking shark cruising slowly with its enormous mouth wide open, seen in side profile. Its open mouth is a HUGE SMOOTH ROUND HOLE like the mouth of a barrel, WITH NO TEETH ANYWHERE - not one tooth, not a single fang, no jagged edge, only pale feathery combs inside. Five VAST GILL SLITS wrap almost the whole way around its head like a stack of collars, nearly meeting on top. A blunt conical snout, tiny eyes, a heavy grey-brown body far bulkier than a hunting shark's, and a crescent tail. This is a harmless slow filter feeder, NOT a great white, NOT a predator, NO teeth
goblinshark: A goblin shark in side profile, a soft flabby PALE PINK deep-sea shark. Its snout is a LONG FLAT BLADE sticking straight out in front, AS LONG AS THE WHOLE REST OF ITS HEAD, jutting far past its mouth like the blade of a paddle. Beneath and behind that blade its NEEDLE-TOOTHED JAWS ARE THRUST RIGHT OUT AND FORWARD, hanging clear of the face like a separate grabbing beak, the way a moray's inner jaws shoot out. Small dark eyes, soft flabby body, small low fins, a long tail with almost no lower lobe
greenlandshark: A Greenland shark in side profile, a massive sluggish shark shaped like a THICK CIGAR - round and heavy and blunt all the way along, with no waist and no streamlining. Its snout is SHORT AND ROUNDED like a closed fist. Its dorsal fin is A LOW ROUNDED BUMP no taller than its own eye is wide - a tiny nub, absolutely NOT a tall triangle, NOT a sail, NOT a great white's fin. All of its fins are small, low and rounded. Dull grey-brown skin, very small eyes, a broad heavy tail. Old, soft and bulky, never sleek
